name: Phishing triage
description: Inbound suspicious-email triage. Ingests a user-reported or mailbox-sweep email, enriches headers / URLs / attachments against upstream Sigma references and OCSF Email/URL/File activity classes, suppresses already-seen or known-benign reports, classifies the intent of the remaining cases, and routes the case to a response branch keyed on intent. Portable CACAO v2 + SecOps-NG content-model extensions so operators compile to the orchestrator they already run (n8n, Temporal, LangGraph, or community targets).

__email_id__.description: Identifier of the reported email in the operator's email-security platform (message-id or platform UID).

__report_source__.description: Where the report originated. One of: user_report, mailbox_sweep.

__benign_or_seen__.description: Set by the suppression check: true when the message matches a known-benign sender or an already-seen case fingerprint within the suppression window.

__intent__.description: Classified intent of the message. One of: phishing, credential_harvest, malware_attached, business_email_compromise, unknown.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: ingest report
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Fetch the reported email envelope, headers, body, and attachment metadata from the email-security platform. Accepts both user-reported messages and mailbox-sweep hits; the source is carried in __report_source__ for downstream accounting against the simulation click-rate and suppression-rate metrics.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: enrich headers, URLs, attachments
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Run sender-domain authentication (SPF / DKIM / DMARC), URL reputation against the operator's allow/deny posture, and attachment static analysis. Emits OCSF Email Activity, URL Activity, and File Activity records per indicator; correlates against the Sigma email-related rule references pinned in mappings.yaml.

if-condition--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00.name: known-benign sender or already seen?
if-condition--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00.description: Suppression branch. on_success: the message matches a known-benign sender or an already-seen case fingerprint within the configured suppression window, and we suppress-and-close. on_failure: we proceed to intent classification.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: suppress and close
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Link this report onto the existing case (or onto the known-benign sender record), close it without paging, and account the suppression against the suppression-rate KRI. Reporter receives the acknowledgement they already opted into; no further notifications fan out.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: classify intent
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Apply the operator's intent classifier (rule-based heuristics, ML model, or analyst review per maturity) to the enriched evidence. Emits one of: phishing, credential_harvest, malware_attached, business_email_compromise, unknown. The classifier itself is operator-bound; only the output contract is fixed by this playbook.

switch-condition--c0a17a01-0000-4000-800.name: route on intent
switch-condition--c0a17a01-0000-4000-800.description: Route to the response branch keyed on the classifier output. Each branch is a single response-routing action that hands off to the appropriate downstream playbook or owner team; the bodies of those downstream playbooks are out of scope here.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: response: phishing
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Generic phishing response: quarantine / purge the message across mailboxes that received it, block sender + URL hashes at the email-security gateway, and notify the responsible response team. Records the response action against the phishing MTTR clock.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: response: credential harvest
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Credential-harvest response: quarantine, block landing-page URLs, identify clickers from URL Activity telemetry and force credential reset / step-up on those identities, notify identity team. Feeds the simulation click-rate KPI when the source is a sanctioned phishing simulation.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: response: malware attached
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Malware-attachment response: quarantine, block attachment SHA-256 at the gateway, hand the host-side investigation off to the endpoint owner playbook for any recipient who opened the file (correlated via OCSF File Activity).

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: response: business email compromise
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: BEC response: escalate to the fraud / finance liaison, freeze any pending payment instruction tied to the message, and open an identity-compromise sub-investigation for the impersonated or compromised sender account. Distinguished from generic phishing because the response chain leaves email-security and enters finance and identity; a BEC case routinely trips the NIS2 / DORA reporting clocks, so the response stamps the regulator-notification-overrun KRI and the timeline-completeness KPI alongside the phishing MTTR clock.

action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.name: response: manual review
action--c0a17a01-0000-4000-8000-00000000.description: Unknown-intent branch: route to a human analyst queue with the enriched evidence packet. Manual outcome is fed back as labelled data for the classifier and recorded for telemetry-coverage accounting.

sources: OASIS CACAO v2.0 specification — workflow step types (start, action, if-condition, switch-condition, end), variable conventions, x_ extension namespace
ENISA — Threat Landscape, phishing and social engineering
NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 21(2)(b) — incident handling capability
NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 21(2)(g) — basic cyber-hygiene practices and training
DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Article 18 — classification of ICT-related incidents
DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Article 19 — reporting of major ICT-related incidents
MITRE D3FEND — Message Authentication (d3f:MessageAuthentication), Sender Reputation Analysis (d3f:SenderReputationAnalysis)

OSCAL anchors: NIST 800-53 IR-4 / IR-6 / IR-8 (incident handling, reporting, plan) and AT-2 / AT-3 / AT-4 (awareness, role-based training, training records) — wired through content/controls/ entries control.incident_handling_capability@v1, control.incident_timeline_signals@v1, control.training_attestation@v1, control.phishing_simulation@v1, control.recurring_incident_correlator@v1
OCSF v1.4.0 — Email Activity (class 4009), Email URL Activity (class 4012), File Activity (class 1001)
SigmaHQ — upstream rule provenance for the detection.sigma.email.* references pinned in mappings.yaml (no Sigma rules authored here)
DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Article 17 — ICT-related incident management process (detect, manage, notify); clock signals captured via control.incident_timeline_signals@v1
